chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu al-Maghra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, that he asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about a yard between two houses, so he claimed that Ali (peace be upon him) judged for the owner of the house from whose side the fence was.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on shared yards and fences between two properties?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *qabd* (possession) in determining ownership of shared boundary structures, a key concept in Shia jurisprudence regarding property rights. It highlights how Imam Ali (peace be upon him) established that the side from which the partition is accessible or maintained holds precedence, reflecting the practical application of justice in communal living. This ruling underscores the importance of clear boundaries and mutual respect in Islamic urban planning.
